title: Response of Plunge Pool Morphology Evolution to Gully Head Height of Typical Grassland in the Hilly and Gully Region of the Loess Plateau
content:
Abstract

Gully head retreat is a primary process of gully erosion, and plunge pool development plays a critical role in driving head migration. However, the plunge pool morphological evolution of gullies with different head heights and its controlling factors remain poorly understood on natural vegetation covered slopes. To fill these gaps, in situ scouring experiments were conducted under different gully head heights (0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 m) on one typical natural grassland slope in the hilly and gully region of the Loess Plateau, China. Each test was run for 180 min and the flowing water was stopped at 20-min interval to measure the morphological parameters of the plunge pools by structure from motion photogrammetry. The results showed that jet flow energy increased with gully head height, whereas plunge pool morphology exhibited a different response to head height. Under the present experimental conditions, the plunge pool with a gully head height of 0.8 m was relatively wider, flatter and more regular. Contrast, for the other four gully head heights, the plunge pools were deeper and more complex. Gully head height influenced plunge pool morphology evolution indirectly through two opposing pathways, including a positive effect via enhanced jet flow hydrodynamics and a negative effect associated with differences in soil properties. Plunge pool evolution was governed by the coupled effects of jet flow hydraulics and soil erodibility under natural vegetation conditions. This study provides new insights into the mechanisms of plunge pool morphology evolution and improves the understanding of gully erosion processes in semi-arid ecosystems.
